sites.title: UQAM_4 Saint-Rémi, Quebec (45.2459N, 73.6823W)
desc: It is a transformed forested peatland near Saint-Rémi that is used as an agricultural site. The station has two parts: a fixed tower on the berm at the edge of the field, powered by AC, that carries the EC system and part of the meteorological sensors, and a rover tripod on a trailer inside the field, powered by a solar panel, that carries the radiation, snow and soil sensors. The trailer is moved out of the field for planting and harvest, so the outgoing radiation and soil data do not represent the field during those periods.

items.v: A dynamic canopy that varies between no plants to 40cm height ones. It needs modelling to rerun the flux calculations.

sites.title: UQAM_5 Saint-François-du-Lac, Quebec (46.0886N, 72.9174W)
desc: It is a natural marsh near Saint-François-du-Lac that floods every spring, with water reaching up to 3 m in extreme events. The station sits on two wooden platforms on certified screw piles 3 m above the ground: one for the solar panels and battery bank, the other for the scaffolding tower and equipment. Access may require a boat during floods and a couple of kilometres of walking in winter.

sections.h: Winter shutdown of the water sensors

items.v: At every site the CS456 pressure transducers (WTD) and the EasyProbe water multiprobes are disconnected for the winter, because they get damaged when the water gets close to 0 °C.
not a measurement: exclude it in first stage, one dated window per winter
re-measure the CS456 depth and add a new dated calibration row; the previous season's datum does not carry over

site_summaries.d: Restored marsh near Lac Saint-Pierre. Access by boat across the marsh; site sits on National Defence land, so visits depend on an access permit.
Disturbed marsh used as an agricultural site (soy). The oldest tower in the network and the reference installation for the others.
Natural open bog (Sphagnum). Solar-powered; access on foot over peat, so a plank boardwalk was added in 2026.
Natural forested bog. Powered by an EFOY methanol fuel-cell hybrid system, which has been the site's main source of trouble.
Disturbed peatland used as an agricultural site (lettuce). Two systems: a fixed AC-powered tower on the berm and a solar rover tripod on a trailer that moves in and out of the field around planting.
Natural marsh that floods each spring (up to 3 m). Newest site: the eddy covariance system was commissioned in August 2026.
